$comment: §12.5 — the gate ledger, as data in the repository.
This file exists because the ledger previously lived only in the dev
database, and dropping that database to test a migration erased every
row in it. §12.5's own words: 'gate status recorded only in a document
drifts from reality within days'. A ledger that lives only in a mutable
database drifts faster, and silently — nothing tells you it is gone.
Here it is reviewable in git, reconstructible with `make gates`, and it
moves in the same commit as the code whose gate it describes. The
verification_runs table remains the queryable form; this is its source.
passed    — the gate is closed. Requires evidenceUrl; the migration
enforces that with a CHECK constraint, not a convention.
executed  — the check ran green, but §15 classes the gate as G -> X or
E, so it cannot close without a live environment or a third
party. Recording these as 'passed' is exactly the lie the
clock: A = generation, B = execution, C = external (§15).

gates.notes: packages/db/test/geography.test.ts — the hand-written EWKB parser round-trips against real PostGIS ST_X/ST_Y. lng/lat ordering is asserted explicitly: transposed, Johannesburg lands in Somalia.

§12.2 — N locums race one shift against real Postgres row locks; the partial unique index bookings_one_confirmed_per_shift is the backstop. Mutation-checked: dropping FOR UPDATE produces unique violations.
§11.5 — replayed keys return the cached response; a replayed key with a different body is rejected rather than silently answered.
§12.1 — Argon2id, refresh rotation, reuse detection, session watermark invalidation.
§12.1 — per-IP login limiting, tighter than the global limit.
Closes the hole where confirmBooking never checked pharmacy membership. Enforced in packages/core rather than middleware, so the worker is covered too.
§11.5 — X-Twilio-Signature validated over the full signed URL; unsigned requests rejected.
§12.1 — the malicious-upload fixture set. Stub scanner only detects EICAR; assertProductionReady refuses to boot production with it.
§8 — check-in/check-out windows. Anti-spoofing needs physical Android hardware (§16) and is not covered here.
§5 — document review queue and the verified-vs-complete distinction.
Self-service profile editing for both sides.
§9 — the R10 accountability fee rides the month's subscription rather than triggering its own transaction.
§11.3 — business-initiated is always a template, with no exception for a recently-open session window.
§11.4 — opt-out always wins, compared by timestamp so re-opt-in is handled.
§4.4 — deferred to 07:00 SAST, never dropped. booking_cancelled deliberately ignores quiet hours.
§11.6 — the cap alerts and does not block; a cap that suppressed booking confirmations would turn a billing anomaly into an outage.
§11.7 — a 'sent' event with no delivery confirmation is not evidence anything reached anyone.

§2/§0.2 — decline, retry, outage and timeout-after-settlement against the fake provider. Money moves exactly once; an outage does not burn a retry attempt. §15 requires a Payfast sandbox driven into error states to close it.

§4.4 — packages/core/test/gates/drain.test.ts against real Postgres: exactly-once claim under two concurrent workers, batch size honoured, opt-out re-checked at send time, failed sends terminal, stalled claims surfaced rather than reclaimed. Mutation-checked — removing `skip locked` fails the contention test with a named assertion. Executed, not passed: the fake sender proves the claim protocol, not the Twilio integration.

apps/worker/test/scheduler.test.ts against real Redis and real Postgres: a dispatched job moves a real row, an unhandled job name fails loudly, stale schedules are reconciled away on boot, re-registering does not double the cadence.

§6/§14 — 17 tests in packages/core/test/gates/disintermediation.test.ts. Mechanism is asserted hard: every rule fires, the false positives §14 names by hand do not, a flagged message is still delivered verbatim, the flag is invisible to participants, and the time gate refuses non-participants and threads closed 72h after the shift. Accuracy is reported and deliberately NOT asserted — §15: 'the number does not exist until measured', and the corpus labels were written by the same process that wrote the regexes. Provisional over 220 messages: 47 TP / 0 FP / 171 TN / 2 FN. The gate cannot close until reviewed:true appears in the corpus (§16 human labelling, Phase 1).

apps/web driven end-to-end in a real Chromium against the running API and a seeded Postgres: manager signs in, posts a radius shift, a locum 30km away sees it and applies, the manager confirms, both message through the platform. Verified in the browser that localStorage, sessionStorage and document.cookie are all empty — the BFF keeps every token server-side. Two real defects found by doing this, both fixed and regression-tested: a raw Postgres constraint name reaching the user on duplicate apply, and confirmBooking never checking §5 verification.

§7 — 18 tests. §7 is one line in the spec, so the interpretation is written into tiers.ts rather than assumed. Four anonymisation controls, each asserted by behaviour: a distinct-rater floor, a dominance guard (a pharmacy booking the same locum weekly is one opinion), delta protection (an aggregate that refreshes on a single new rating lets the subject solve for it), and a density rule that withholds outright where the local market is too thin for any k to hide a rater. Two errors found and corrected while building: the density formula scaled the floor the opposite way to its own comment, and unratedBookingsFor prompted only the locum — collecting one-directional ratings under the word 'unified'. Both mutation-checked.

§0.1 Phase 0 exit criterion — 25 tests (17 in packages/observability, 8 in apps/api). Fired for real against the running API with an external HTTP receiver: POST /__drill/boom returned 500 and delivered a severity=page alert. Negatives confirmed live in the same run — cooldown 429, bad secret 401, unauthenticated tRPC 401, and ZERO alerts delivered for those three. Two defects found while building: DrillGate refused its own first firing (lastFiredAt=0 read as 'fired at the epoch', invisible under a real clock), and classify() paged on every tRPC UNAUTHORIZED because tRPC's own errors are not DomainErrors. Cannot move past 'executed': §15 says the gate is that a phone buzzes, which needs staging, a real webhook and someone on call.

§12.2 — the four panels the spec names, counted from rows rather than application counters. 8 tests against the seeded database plus a live render as a real MFA admin: confirmation 16.0% (183/1143), WhatsApp delivery 69.8% (88/126), settlement 62.5% (125/200), proximity query 17.5ms over 269 open shifts and 5001 located locums. Also docs/ONCALL.md — who gets paged, for what, and by when. The page exists mainly to carry the three failures that raise no exception and so can never reach the §0.1 pager: a shift that started unfilled, a deferred message past due, and a charge with no answer from the provider.

§10 — right of access and right to erasure, neither of which existed. popiaConsentAt was a column and nothing more, in a product holding SAPC certificates, ID documents, a GPS trace per shift and message history. 14 tests. The structural guarantee: RETENTION_POLICY is asserted against every pgTable in the schema, so a new table cannot be added without a retention decision, and every table marked delete/anonymise must also appear in the export. That consistency check found a real gap while being written — auth_attempts and favourite_locums were being erased but never disclosed. Erasure deliberately RETAINS no-show and completed-shift counts: clearing them would make the erasure endpoint a §7 reputation reset (three no-shows, delete, re-register, clean record). Anonymisation not deletion, and the UI says so rather than promising a deletion the product does not perform. Legal sufficiency is E-blocked — §15 lists 5 legal opinions.

§12.1 — per-ACCOUNT quotas on browse, booking creation and data export. The existing limit was per-IP, which is right for credential stuffing and wrong for the two threats §12.1 actually names: an authenticated scraper gets a new IP by switching to mobile data, while a pharmacy group behind one NAT shares a bucket. 3 tests, and one of them is a regression: the first version of the middleware returned its own protectedProcedure and silently dropped the locum-only check from applyToShift — a manager could have applied to shifts, with nothing failing visibly. Caught by the compiler noticing locumProcedure had become unused. Postgres-backed rather than Redis so browse does not gain a second way to be down; swept hourly by the worker.

§8/§16 — apps/mobile, the reason Expo was chosen on day one. 9 tests over the pure signal logic in src/lib/attendance.ts. THIS GATE CANNOT CLOSE HERE and §16 says so directly: 'At least one physical Android device with a mock-location app installed and active. Emulator confirmation is explicitly insufficient — the signals being captured are precisely the ones an emulator misrepresents.' What is proven is the half hardware does not decide: Android's mocked flag is forwarded, iOS sends NOTHING rather than a reassuring false (the API distinguishes absent from false, and 'unknowable' recorded as 'clean' would make an iPhone record look better-evidenced than an honest Android one), no distance is computed on the device, and anomalies annotate without ever refusing a check-in. location.ts is deliberately thin so the untestable surface is as small as possible.

§11.1 — the real WhatsAppSender. 11 tests against a real HTTP server standing in for Twilio: exact request shape, Basic auth, ContentVariables in Meta's one-based positional form, StatusCallback present, error classification (429/5xx/408 transient, 63016 permanent), timeout, and refusal to send a template with no approved Content SID rather than falling back to free-form. Found that FakeWhatsAppSender had been LYING: it returns priceCents on every send, and Twilio returns price:null on accept and bills later on the status callback — any code assuming a send-time price would pass every test and report zero §11.6 spend in production. Also: Twilio reports price as a negative decimal, which stored verbatim makes daily spend a growing negative number and the cap never fires. Cannot close — §15 lists the sender and template approval as externally blocked, so no message here has ever reached a phone.
